scope: Who wins the contracts that external loans pay for. Covers (1) World Bank contract-award notices for the largest India investment projects since 2000 — EDFC I–III (DFCCIL), POWERGRID PSDP IV–V, National Ganga (NMCG), NHIIP (MoRTH), Vishnugad Pipalkoti (THDC), PMGSY, NRLP, RWSS — 370 notices read from the Bank's procurement-notices API, with awarded firm, country, price, method, date and, where the notice publishes them, every losing bidder and price; (2) the World Bank Listing of Ineligible Firms — every India-country debarment from 2010 to 2026, with the cited ground and period, as enforce claims; (3) ADB-financed Delhi–Meerut RRTS awards from ADB's Procurement Plan, the STEC Package 4 episode and the July 2020 GFR Order; (4) a symmetry check against the domestic Union awards register. Awards are recorded borrower/implementing agency → supplier; suppliers are resolved to existing co:/energy: ids where they are graph companies, to fin:<slug> with resolved:true where the Bank/ADB record gives the awardee's name (JVs and consortia are recorded under the JV name the record gives and flagged collisionRisk where members are not expanded), and resolved:false with no claims where only a group name appears (Shapoorji Pallonji). Leaves out: loan terms (in worldbank.json / adb-aiib.json), JICA-financed WDFC awards (Japanese tied procurement, noted in the DFCCIL entity), state-level lender-funded awards, and the ministers at approval. Amounts are contract prices in ₹ crore straight from INR-denominated notices (no conversion); ADB package values are US$ estimates converted at ≈₹73.5/US$ and marked estimated.

narratives.claim: The Modi government handed a Chinese state firm a ₹1,126 crore Delhi–Meerut tunnel contract while Indian soldiers were dying at Galwan.
narratives.strongestCase: The facts of the award are established: STEC, a Chinese SOE, was L1 on 2020-06-12 (three days before the Galwan clash), the government's own July 2020 Order was meant to keep such bidders out of public procurement, and NCRTC nonetheless issued the LOA on 2020-12-09 while the LAC standoff continued (National Herald framing).

NCRTC: 'awarded following the set procedure and guidelines'.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A DoE/ADB record showing India sought and was refused STEC's exclusion, or a waiver granted specifically for this package, would move it to 'well-supported' as a lender-constraint story; evidence that NCRTC had discretion to reject the L1 and chose not to would move it toward the critics.

symmetryCheck: Lens: 'who wins, how concentrated, how many bid, how often single-source' applied to the lender-funded family and to the domestic Union register (research/raw/tenders-centre.json, 88 awards 2019–2026). Lender-funded: top winner by value L&T 20.3% (WB) / 35.1% (ADB RRTS); top five 62.5%; mean 5.6 bidders where published, 0 single-bid awards, 2.2% direct selection (consultancies only). Domestic: top winner by count Adani group 17/88 (19%); by value PSU-GoI 30.5% and Reliance 26.0% (spectrum auctions dominate); bidder counts known for 16/88 (mean 4.25); no sole-bidder awards flagged; 59/88 are auctions where 'concentration' is a revenue-share outcome, not a contract. Reading: lender-funded procurement shows more published competition and a lower observed top-winner share than the domestic register, but the domestic register's bidder data are so sparse that the difference is partly one of disclosure. The lens produces an 'L&T dominates' picture for lender money and an 'Adani/Reliance dominate' picture for domestic money; both dissolve on inspection into a handful of pre-qualifiable firms splitting large packages by L1, and neither register contains a documented single-bidder award. The alarming-looking fact common to both is opacity after award, not rigging before it.
